Credential precedence for Cloud commands:

1. `--api-ke
y` — must be an `sk_` key. A `mcpjam_…` legacy key is a usage error.\n2. `MCPJAM_API_KEY` — same `sk_` rule. A legacy value in thi
s env var is ignored (with a warning) so SDK eval reporting can still use it.\n3. Stored OAuth from `mcpjam cloud login`\n4. Missi
ng — Cloud commands fail with login guidance before they hit the network (`mcpjam cloud status` reports `missing` instead)\n\nAPI

URL precedence:

1. `--api-url`
2. `MCPJAM_API_URL`, or `MCPJAM_BASE_URL` (the same server without `/api/v1`)
3. The server sa
ved with the OAuth login (only when that login is the credential; a login saved before logins recorded their server counts as MCPJ

am Cloud, and one whose recorded server is not a usable address is refused with exit `3`)
4. `https://app.mcpjam.com/api/v1`

E
very command that can contact MCPJam (it accepts `--api-url`, or it uploads results) decides its server when it starts, before it
contacts anything. An explicit `--api-url`, `MCPJAM_API_URL` or `MCPJAM_BASE_URL` that is not an `http(s)` URL, or that carries cr
edentials, a query or a fragment, is a usage error (exit `2`), and so are the two variables naming different servers. The error ma
sks credentials, a query and a fragment, and does not repeat a value that is not a URL. A saved login is only sent to its own serv
er: when it is the credential and the order picks another server, the command exits `3` before any request. `mcpjam cloud status`
uses the same checks but stays network-free: it still emits the complete JSON report, sets `ok: false`, includes `credential.valid
` / `deployment.valid` plus an `error` string, and exits `1`. Missing credentials are informational (`credential.valid: null`) and
successful.\n\nSuccessful Cloud commands print an audience line to stderr (`Using MCPJam Cloud as … · project: … · <apiUrl>`). `-

-quiet` suppresses it. Machine-readable JSON stays on stdout. `cloud status` redacts API keys.

## Cloud project scope

Most C

loud commands pick one project:

1. `--project <id-or-name>`
2. An explicit `project` field in `--file` / `--json`
3. `MCPJAM_

PROJECT`
4. The nearest valid `.mcpjam/project.json`
5. Automatic — the most recently updated project you can see

Empty `--pr
oject` or `MCPJAM_PROJECT` is a usage error. `MCPJAM_PROJECT_ID` does **not** select a Cloud CLI project (it is SDK eval reporting

only).

```bash theme={"theme":"css-variables"}
mcpjam cloud login
mcpjam cloud link # writes .mcpjam/pr
oject.json (no secrets)\nmcpjam cloud status # zero-network: credential, deployment, selector\nmcpjam cloud eval li

st # uses the link
mcpjam cloud link --remove
```

`mcpjam cloud eval` run-inspection commands (`status`, `cancel`
, `judge`, `iterations`, `gate`, `compare`, `trace`, `steps`, `screenshot`, `video`) follow the same rule — `--project` is optiona
l. `mcpjam cloud sessions list` does too; `--all-projects` restores a cross-project listing and cannot be combined with `--project

`. Hosted `readiness` never reads the project link.

## What `--host` means

`--host` is not one flag. The meaning depends on

the command:

| Where | What it selects |
| - | - |
| `server`, `tools`, `resources`, `prompts` | An **AI client** (`claude`,
`chatgpt`, `cursor`, …). The CLI sends that host's `clientInfo`, capabilities, and protocol version in `initialize`. |\n| `test --
host` | One host **template** to emulate for a local suite run: its handshake, tool visibility and model settings. Never the real
client. |\n| `compat --host` | Which AI clients to report. Repeatable; default is all. |\n| `cloud eval --host`, `cloud goals`, `c
loud studies` | A **saved project Host** (`<id-or-name>`), the client config an eval or goal run is stamped with. |\n| `cloud envi
ronments --host-id` | The project Host id the environment runs as. Distinct from eval's `--host`. |\n\n`--host` on a local command
is mutually exclusive with `--client-capabilities`. A Cloud `--host` is mutually exclusive with `--server` / `--environment` when

those already supply a closed server set.

## Global flags

These flags apply to every command. Cloud credentials `--api-key`

/ `--api-url` are declared on `mcpjam cloud`, not the program root.

| Flag | Default | Description |
| - | - | - |
| `--time
out <ms>` | `30000` | Request timeout in milliseconds |\n| `--rpc` | off | Include raw JSON-RPC request/response logs in JSON outp
ut under `_rpcLogs` |\n| `--quiet` | off | Suppress non-result progress output on stderr |\n| `--no-telemetry` | off | Disable ano
nymous telemetry for this invocation |\n| `--format <format>` | `human` on TTY, `json` when piped | Raw output format (`json` or `

human`) |
| `-v, --version` | | Print the CLI version |

## Output formats

The CLI auto-detects whether stdout is a terminal
:\n\n* **Interactive terminal** — defaults to `--format human`. For most commands this is pretty-printed JSON; `server doctor` and
the OAuth conformance commands provide dedicated human-readable summaries.\n* **Piped or redirected** (CI, `| jq`, agent invocati
on) — defaults to `--format json`, the full structured result.\n* **Conformance in CI** — `protocol conformance`, `protocol confor
mance-suite`, `oauth conformance`, `oauth conformance-suite`, `apps conformance`, and `apps conformance-suite` support `--reporter

junit-xml` and `--reporter json-summary`.
* **Explicit `--format`** always wins over the auto-detected default.

**For agents*
*: raw JSON is the source of truth. Human format is a lossy presentation layer. If you're parsing output programmatically, pass `-
-quiet --format json`.\n\nJSON-valued flags accept inline JSON, `@path`, or `-` for stdin. `tools call` also accepts `--tool-args-
stdin` as a shorthand for `--tool-args -`. Use files or stdin for large payloads to avoid shell escaping issues:\n\n```bash theme=
{\"theme\":\"css-variables\"}\necho '{\"key\":\"value\"}' | mcpjam tools call --url $URL --access-token $TOKEN \\\n --tool-name m

y_tool --tool-args - --quiet --format json
```

## Connecting to servers

The CLI supports two transport modes, selected by w

hich flags you pass:

* `--url ...` selects HTTP.
* `--command ...` selects stdio.
* `--transport http|stdio` is optional and
acts as an explicit override/validator when you want the CLI to reject mismatched flags early.\n\n### HTTP (Streamable HTTP / SSE)

```bash theme={"theme":"css-variables"}
mcpjam server doctor --url https://your-server.com/mcp
```

Add auth when need

ed:

```bash theme={"theme":"css-variables"}
# Static bearer token
mcpjam server doctor --url https://your-server.com/mcp

--access-token $TOKEN

# OAuth tokens from a prior login
mcpjam server doctor --url https://your-server.com/mcp --oauth-access-

token $TOKEN

# Custom headers
mcpjam server doctor --url https://your-server.com/mcp --header "X-API-Key: $KEY"
```

###

```

Stdio child processes inherit the parent shell environment by default. Use
`-e/-
-env` to add values or override inherited ones for the spawned server.\nStructured debug artifacts only record the explicit env ke

ys you pass through
`-e/--env`; inherited shell variables are not enumerated.

> [!NOTE]

re HTTP-only command groups. They do

## Update notifications

After a successful command, the CL

I checks whether a newer version of `@mcpjam/cli` is available and prints a notice to stderr when one is found:

```
Update ava

ilable: @mcpjam/cli 1.2.0 -> 1.3.0
Run npm install -g @mcpjam/cli to update
```

The check is non-blocking: version data is fe
tched in a detached background process and cached locally for 24 hours, so it never slows down your commands. The notice is writte
n to stderr only and never touches stdout or JSON output, so it is safe for both interactive terminals and AI agents (Claude Code,
Cursor, etc.) that capture stderr. It is suppressed automatically in CI.\n\nTo opt out, set one of these environment variables be

fore running any command:

| Variable | Effect |
| - | - |
| `MCPJAM_NO_UPDATE_CHECK=1` | Disable update checks for `@mcpjam/c
